title: Head of Americas Internal Audit
description: Head of Americas Internal Audit Who we are About Stripe Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career. About the team Stripe Internal Audit provides the Board and management with independent, risk-based assurance, advice, insight, and foresight designed to strengthen Stripe’s ability to create, protect, and sustain value What you’ll do The Head of Americas Internal Audit will lead the strategy, organization, and execution of Stripe’s operational audit portfolio across the Americas. Reporting to the Global Head of Internal Audit and serving as a member of the Internal Audit leadership team, this leader will provide an independent perspective on the risks arising from Stripe’s evolving payments, money movement, financial services, platform, and technology-enabled business models. The role is accountable for developing a high-performing regional audit organization; translating Stripe’s strategy, enterprise risks, and legal entity obligations into a multi-year audit strategy; and delivering clear, timely insight to senior management, the Stripe, Inc. Audit Committee, and relevant regulated entity boards. The leader will partner closely with Technology Audit, Data Analytics, Professional Practices, and Global Licensing Enablement to deliver an integrated global audit program. At Stripe’s request, the individual may also serve as Head of Audit for one or more Americas legal entities. Responsibilities Set the strategy, vision, and operating model for operational audit across the Americas, translating Stripe’s company strategy, enterprise risk assessment, regulatory obligations, and legal entity risk profiles into a multi-year strategy and annual risk-based audit portfolio; anticipate emerging risks and regulatory developments across the US, Canada, Latin America, and the broader financial services ecosystem, adapting coverage as Stripe’s products and legal entity footprint evolve Lead and scale a multifaceted regional organization, including organizational design, hiring, succession planning, leadership development, performance management, and deployment of talent across the highest-priority risks Own the quality and results of the Americas audit portfolio, including risk assessment, planning, issue severity and escalation, reporting, remediation oversight, and timely delivery against approved plans; promote strong governance and accountability, including clear ownership and timely remediation of significant issues, while maintaining alignment with applicable professional standards and Stripe Internal Audit methodology Provide an independent risk perspective to senior management, the Stripe, Inc. Audit Committee, and relevant Americas legal entity boards; communicate complex issues clearly and influence durable improvements; represent Internal Audit with regulators, external auditors, bank partners, and other assurance providers, as appropriate, maintaining trusted relationships while preserving Internal Audit’s independence Coordinate with Internal Audit’s functional leaders in Technology Audit, Data Analytics, Professional Practices, and Global Licensing Enablement to ensure integrated coverage and avoid duplicative or fragmented assurance Direct risk-based assurance across Stripe’s evolving business models, including payments, platforms, money movement and treasury, lending and credit, crypto and stablecoins, consumer products, and other emerging products and commercial models; evaluate the effectiveness of governance and controls relating to financial crime, consumer protection, safeguarding and reconciliation, credit and financial risk, operational resilience, cybersecurity and data, model and artificial intelligence (AI) risk, third-party and bank-partner dependencies, and financial reporting Modernize the audit function through data analytics, automation, continuous risk sensing, and responsible use of AI, in partnership with the Head of Data Analytics Who you are We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement. title: Head of Internal Audit
description: About Faire Faire is a technology wholesale platform built on the belief that the future is local. Independent retailers around the globe collectively represent a multi-hundred-billion-dollar wholesale market that has historically been fragmented and offline. At Faire, we're using the power of tech, data, and machine learning to connect this thriving community of entrepreneurs across the globe. Picture your favorite boutique in town — we help them discover the best products from around the world to sell in their stores. With the right tools and insights, we believe that we can level the playing field so businesses can grow and local communities can thrive. We’re looking for smart, resourceful and passionate people to join us as we power the shop local movement. If you believe in community, come join ours. About this role We're looking for a Head of Internal Audit to build Faire's Internal Audit function and lead our SOX (financial controls) program as we prepare for public company requirements. You’ll partner with process owners across the company to make sure our key controls are well designed, operating effectively, and supported by complete and accurate data. This role owns the audit plan, is an independent voice on risk and controls, and partners closely with the Audit Committee. You'll inherit a small SOX team and shape how it's structured as Internal Audit grows, with scope that may expand into areas like enterprise risk management. You'll also help govern how Faire builds and uses AI, and use data and AI to make audit faster and more continuous. As Finance and the business rebuild workflows around AI, you’ll make sure those workflows are SOX compliant by design: advising on controls throughout the build process, setting the standard for evidence and review, and giving the Audit Committee and our external auditor confidence in the results. You understand our technology environment, have built or scaled an audit function at a fast-growing tech company, and are ready to roll up your sleeves. You see the Internal Audit function as a partner to the business, not a checkpoint. This role reports to the CAO, with a functional reporting line to the CFO and the Audit Committee of the Board. What you’ll do  Build and lead Faire's Internal Audit function, including the audit plan, team, and outside partners Lead our SOX team and own the SOX program, including readiness for our first external audit of internal controls Review controls over our technology: cloud, software changes, system access, data, and cybersecurity Provide independent assurance over how Faire builds and uses AI, including model errors, bias, and privacy Modernize audit with data analytics, automation, and responsible AI to test more and monitor continuously Give the Audit Committee and executives a clear, candid view of risk and control health Partner with Finance, Legal, Security, Privacy, and Engineering to advise on controls early for new products, systems, and expansion Track issues to closure and push for root-cause fixes Hire, coach, and develop the team and manage outside audit partners Take on special projects, analysis, and reporting as needed Qualifications Bachelor's degree in accounting, finance, information systems, or a related field, plus at least one of CPA, CIA, CISA, or CISSP 12+ years in audit and risk, including 6+ reviewing IT and financial controls and 3+ leading teams Deep SOX experience, including IPO readiness or first-year external auditor review of internal controls Strong understanding of the technology environment, including IT controls, cloud, data, and cybersecurity Working knowledge of AI risk and governance, including generative and agentic AI, and experience using AI or analytics in audit Knowledge of US GAAP, COSO, PCAOB, and IIA standards Experience presenting to Audit Committees, boards, and senior executives Experience selecting audit and risk technology Experience building an internal audit function at a tech company; hyper-growth or marketplace experience is a plus Strong communicator with sound judgment in ambiguous situations Resourceful and not afraid to roll up your sleeves Salary range: San Francisco: The salary range for this role is $200,000 - $275,000 per year. This role will also be eligible for equity and benefits. Actual base pay will be determined based on permissible factors such as transferable skills, work experience, market demands, and primary work location. The base pay range provided is subject to change and may be modified in the future.   Hybrid Faire employees currently go into the office 3 days per week on Tuesdays, Thursdays, and a third flex day of their choosing (Monday, Wednesday, or Friday). Additionally, hybrid in-office roles will have the flexibility to work remotely up to 4 weeks per year. Specific Workplace and Information Technology positions may require onsite attendance 5 days per week as will be indicated in the job posting.  Why you’ll love working at

title: Director/Senior Director, New Products
description: About Us Fieldguide is establishing a new state of trust for global commerce and capital markets through automating and streamlining the work of advisory, audit, and tax practitioners at the world's largest CPA firms. Put simply, we build software for the people who enable trust between businesses. We're based in San Francisco, CA, but built as a remote-first company that enables you to do your best work from anywhere. We're backed by top investors including Goldman Sachs, Bessemer Venture Partners, 8VC, and Y Combinator. We value diversity, in backgrounds and in experiences. We need people from all backgrounds and walks of life to help build the future of audit and advisory. Fieldguide's team is inclusive, driven, humble, and supportive. We are deliberate and self-reflective about the kind of team and culture we are building, seeking teammates who are not only strong in their own aptitudes but care deeply about supporting each other's growth. As a growth stage startup employee, you'll have the opportunity to build the future of business trust. We make audit practitioners' lives easier by eliminating up to 50% of their work and giving them better work-life balance. If you share our values and enthusiasm for building a great culture and product, you will find a home at Fieldguide. About the Role You will be the Director/Senior Director of Fieldguide's internal audit product: own the P&L, set the strategy, and take it from first design partners to a repeatable, multi-million-dollar business. Internal audit teams carry the same capacity problem as external auditors, often with smaller budgets: rising SOX and regulatory scope, new risk areas like AI, cyber and third parties, and a shrinking talent pool. Much of their work (walkthroughs, controls testing, evidence requests, workpapers, issue tracking) looks like the work Fieldguide's agents already execute for audit firms. This role takes that engine to a new buyer: Chief Audit Executives and internal audit leaders at corporations, plus the firms that deliver co-sourced and outsourced internal audit for them. This is not a product management or a sales role. You will make the calls a founder makes: which internal audit workflows to attack first, which companies are the first customers, what to build next and what to kill. You will have a dedicated pod of engineers, designers and internal audit subject-matter experts, and the full weight of Fieldguide's platform, brand and firm relationships behind you. What You'll Do Find the wedge. Spend real time inside internal audit functions with CAEs, audit directors, SOX program leads and staff auditors. Identify the high-volume, high-pain work (SOX controls testing, walkthroughs, evidence collection, risk assessments, operational audits) where an agent can do the job end to end, and decide which problem we win first. Build the product with the pod. Partner with engineering, and design leads and our internal audit SMEs to define what ships, in what order, and what "good enough" means for work that lands in front of audit committees and external auditors. Write the spec when needed; sit in the eval reviews. Land design partners, then customers. Help close the first 5–10 internal audit teams. Turn them into referenceable deployments with measurable hours saved, coverage gained and quality improved. Partner with GTM. Work with Sales, Marketing and Customer Success to shape how the product is positioned, sold and expanded: into corporate IA teams directly and through co-sourcing firms already on Fieldguide. Bring the customer insight and proof points they need, and help build a playbook they can run without you. Know the landscape. Understand where incumbent GRC and audit-management tools stop, and position Fieldguide as the system that does the work, not just tracks it. Build the team. Hire the first dedicated GTM, deployment and IA SME roles for the line as it scales. Know when to double down or stop. Run tight experiments, read the signal honestly, and bring the company a clear recommendation. Who You Are 8+ years of experience, including at least one stint taking a product or business from zero to one: as a founder, a GM of a new line, or the first operator on a new product at a high-growth company. Real P&L or revenue ownership, with numbers you can talk through. Strong commercial instinct: you have sold complex B2B software to senior, skeptical buyers and closed deals yourself. Enough technical depth to work as a peer with AI engineers: you understand what agents can and can't do today, and how evals and human review fit in. Clear, structured writing. You turn ambiguity into a crisp memo and a plan people can act on. Bonus Points Background in internal audit, SOX, risk or controls: as a practitioner or leader in a corporate IA function, in a Big Four or Top 100 firm's risk advisory or internal audit practice, or selling into CAEs. CIA or CPA a plus. Experience at a vertical SaaS, GRC or AI-native company between Series B and pre-IPO. Management consulting, investment or strategy background paired with hands-on operating experience. More About Fieldguide Fieldguide is a values-based company. Our values are: Fearless: Inspire and break down seemingly impossible walls. Fast: Launch fast with excellence, iterate to perfection. Lovable: Deliver happiness and 11 star experiences. Owners: Execute and run the business with ownership. Win-win: Create mutual value and earn trust for life. Inclusive: Scale the best ideas with inclusive teams. Benefits Competitive compensation packages with meaningful ownership Flexible PTO 401k Wellness benefits, including a bundle of free therapy sessions Technology and Work from Home reimbursement
